newsitem.title: USA: Lube oil spill slows shipping on Houston channel.
newsitem.headline: Lube oil spill slows shipping on Houston channel.

text.p: Shipping was slowed along a stretch of the Houston Ship Channel on Monday following a weekend lube oil spill at Exxon Corp's Baytown, Texas refinery, a U.S. Coast Guard spokeswoman said.

"We are requesting a slow bell for vessels passing the Exxon Baytown refinery," said Coast Guard Lt. Elizabeth Becker, referring to a request that ships proceed as slowly as possible through the area to keep wakes to a minimum.

An estimated 450 barrels of light lube oil were spilled into the channel at about 1620 CST Sunday after two tanks overflowed while cargo was being transferred onto the tankship Oriental Amethyst, the Coast Guard said.
Operations at the 418,000 barrel per day refinery were unaffected, an Exxon spokesman said.
Sietemar SA, owner of the Panamanian-flagged 357-foot, 5,979 gross ton tanker, assumed responsibility for the spill and contracted for clean-up, the Coast Guard said.
About 200 barrels of lube oil were recovered by booms in the channel, and up to 100 barrels have reached the southern end of Alexander Island, the Coast Guard said.
